newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1997 budget to forecast growth at 2.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: French 1997 budget to forecast growth at 2.3 pct.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Friday the 1997 budget would forecast growth at 2.3 percent.
"The growth assumption which I have retained is 2.3 percent," he told a news conference.
He also said he believed France would have growth of 1.3 percent in 1996, as forecast in the 1996 budget. "I maintain the forecast of 1.3 percent growth," he said. mmd/pnt
The 1997 budget will increase taxes on alcohol and tobacco to help fund the welfare system, Arthuis said.
Petrol duties would be increased in line with inflation, he said, but there would be additional taxes on alcohol and tobacco.
"There will be a tax on tobacco and on alcohol," he said. "As regards petrol duties, we will take account of inflation."
He declined to say how much money would be raised through the extra taxes.
But Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said these would raise a "significant sum".

Official sources have said previuously while the rise in petrol duties would be limited to the rate of inflation, duties on alcohol and tobacco could rise further, given the implications on public health.
Arthuis reaffirmed that France would cut its total budget defict to four percent of gross domestic product this year from five percent last year and to three percent next year.
